source_direct_findings: The official model card reports 182M parameters and German ASR support alongside English, French and Spanish.
The official model artifact is 736,665,600 bytes and its LFS/Xet payload identity is SHA-256 7b97de18b718ef01bf3398715ce8d18486c4d83961e230230b26f5712e112675.
The official model card reports German WER 4.81 on MLS and 5.94 on Mozilla Common Voice 16.1 under its stated evaluation protocol.
The official model card reports experimental word-level and segment-level timestamp support for German.

The official model card reports throughput of 1233 RTFx on A100 and 2041 RTFx on H100 for its OpenASR profiling setup; those are throughput measurements, not Frankenstein conversational endpoint or first-partial latency.
Current NVIDIA NeMo ASR documentation states that Canary models support chunked and streaming inference, but no clay-direct-dev execution was performed in this source stage.
project_inferences_not_runtime_facts: At 182M parameters and a 737 MB reference checkpoint, Canary-180M-Flash is a high-value small-footprint challenger for the German LOCAL-SOLO ASR lane.

Its small model and strong reported batch throughput may reduce ASR resource pressure relative to larger current candidates, but NeMo/PyTorch process overhead can erase part of that advantage and must be measured as whole-process RSS/VRAM on clay-direct-dev.

Official benchmark WER does not establish WER/CER on Frankenstein's conversational German corpus, partial-hypothesis stability, pause handling, barge-in behavior, cancellation correctness or speech-end-to-first-usable-text latency.
Timestamp support is relevant to turn bookkeeping but remains target-runtime behavior until exercised under the selected inference path.
counterhypothesis: The NeMo runtime footprint, decoder/streaming behavior or conversational German error distribution can make Canary-180M-Flash slower or less useful in the actual duplex loop than its parameter count and batch RTFx suggest.

downstream_noncanonical_portability_sign.claim: A community GGUF port exists with F32/F16/Q8/Q6/Q5/Q4 artifacts and reports LibriSpeech test-clean parity-like WER across those quantizations.
downstream_noncanonical_portability_sign.boundary: This downstream port is not NVIDIA official evidence, its quoted WER is English LibriSpeech rather than German, and it receives zero Frankenstein runtime or German-quality credit here. It may be investigated under a separate semantic objective if target hardware favors native GGUF execution.
